title: The Pig War: When One Pig Nearly Started a War (1859)
description:
The Pig War of 1859 really happened: an American farmer shot a British company's pig on San Juan Island, and America and Britain ended up facing each other with soldiers, cannons and warships. The true story, explained in 4 minutes.

Sources:
- US National Park Service, San Juan Island National Historical Park, "The Pig War": https://www.nps.gov/sajh/learn/historyculture/the-pig-war.htm
- Wikipedia, "Pig War (1859)": https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig_War_(1859)

Chapters:
0:00 One pig, two countries
0:21 The border problem
1:01 June 15, 1859: the pig
1:23 $10 or $100?
1:43 The army arrives
2:08 Warships and cannons
2:30 The admiral says no
3:02 12 years of waiting
3:27 A German emperor decides
3:59 Who won?

On June 15, 1859, farmer Lyman Cutlar shot a pig belonging to Charles Griffin of the Hudson's Bay Company. He offered $10; Griffin wanted $100. Captain George Pickett landed with about 65 soldiers, and within weeks 461 Americans with 14 cannons faced five British warships. Rear Admiral Robert Baynes refused to start a war "over a squabble about a pig". Both sides then shared the island for 12 years, until Kaiser Wilhelm I's arbitration gave it to the United States in 1872. The only casualty was the pig.
